```python
import io
import sys

import pytest

from rich.console import Console
from rich.text import Text


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "nerd_font_char, expected_width",
    [
        # This is the character specifically mentioned in the bug report
        ("\U000f024d", 1),  # nf-fa-folder_download
        # Add a few more common Nerd Font icons that should be single width
        ("\U000f0002", 1),  # nf-fa-github
        ("\U000e7ad", 1),  # nf-dev-git
        ("\U000e795", 1),  # nf-dev-python
        ("\U000e7b5", 1),  # nf-dev-nodejs
    ],
)
def test_nerd_font_character_width(nerd_font_char: str, expected_width: int) -> None:
    """
    Test that specific Nerd Font characters are correctly identified as single width.
    """
    console = Console(
        file=io.StringIO(),
        width=80,
        legacy_windows=False,  # Ensure non-legacy Windows rendering path
        force_terminal=True,  # Force terminal rendering to get character width calculations
    )
    text = Text(nerd_font_char)
    # Render the text and check the width of the rendered segments
    segments = list(console.render(text, console.options))
    total_width = sum(segment.cell_length for segment in segments)

    assert (
        total_width == expected_width
    ), f"Nerd Font character '{nerd_font_char}' (U+{ord(nerd_font_char):x}) has unexpected width. Expected {expected_width}, got {total_width}."

```

import io
import sys

import pytest

from rich.console import Console
from rich.text import Text


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "nerd_font_char, expected_width",
    [
        # This is the character specifically mentioned in the bug report
        ("\U000f024d", 1),  # nf-fa-folder_download
        # Add a few more common Nerd Font icons that should be single width
        ("\U000f0002", 1),  # nf-fa-github
        ("\U000e7ad", 1),  # nf-dev-git
        ("\U000e795", 1),  # nf-dev-python
        ("\U000e7b5", 1),  # nf-dev-nodejs
    ],
)
def test_nerd_font_character_width(nerd_font_char: str, expected_width: int) -> None:
    """
    Test that specific Nerd Font characters are correctly identified as single width.
    """
    console = Console(
        file=io.StringIO(),
        width=80,
        legacy_windows=False,  # Ensure non-legacy Windows rendering path
        force_terminal=True,  # Force terminal rendering to get character width calculations
    )
    text = Text(nerd_font_char)
    # Render the text and check the width of the rendered segments
    # The bug is that rich.console.Console.renderable_width() (which is used internally
    # by render() and other methods) incorrectly calculates the width of certain
    # Nerd Font characters as 2 instead of 1.
    # We can directly check the width calculation for the Text object.
    calculated_width = text.__rich_measure__(
        console, console.options
    ).maximum  # Use maximum width for single character
    
    assert (
        calculated_width == expected_width
    ), f"Nerd Font character '{nerd_font_char}' (U+{ord(nerd_font_char):x}) has unexpected width. Expected {expected_width}, got {calculated_width}."
